teaser.text: Cigna is a company that sells ways to pay for, organize and deliver health care. A dollar enters through premiums, employer and health-plan fees, or payments for medicines and care, then leaves for claims, drugs, providers and operating costs; what remains is the business’s profit.

stock.title: Cigna stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Cigna's forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios against pharmacy economics, cash generation, valuation and the Signature transition.
stock.opening: Cigna's weighted share price rises from $303.61 in October 2027 to $368.15 in October 2029, including dividends. The forecast hinges on whether Signature preserves pharmacy economics while cash generation supports each share.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Cigna's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Cigna's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: Cigna’s weighted share price rises from $303.61 in October 2027 to $368.15 in October 2029, including dividends. That means a modest 3% return after one year, followed by 15% after two years and 29% after three years. The 2029 outcomes span $260.14 in the bear case to $486.53 in the bull case, against today’s $301.27 price.

The bear case requires Signature to win clients through concessions while PBM earnings remain pressured. Slower growth and weaker cash conversion restrict buybacks, increase concern about debt and contract economics, and compress the multiple. It produces $284.28 in October 2027 and $260.14 in October 2029, including dividends. Its 28% probability sits above the 25% estimates from the earnings and dividend specialists and near the multiple specialist’s 30%, because the pressure is already visible but does not require an earnings collapse.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Cigna, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case reaches only $9,195 million because PBM pressure and weak cash conversion reduce growth to 2%. Pharmacy Benefit Services income fell 27% in the latest quarter, while first-half operating cash flow was only $710 million. The bull case reaches $11,181 million by applying the 14% high end, assuming Signature scales without lasting margin damage and specialty earnings and savings strengthen. The historical increase in adjusted EPS from $20.47 in 2021 to $29.84 in 2025 supports continued growth, but not the bull outcome by itself.

Persistent concessions or weaker cash conversion justify compression. Successful Signature adoption, specialty growth and modernization savings could instead improve confidence in earnings quality and support expansion.

blocks.heading: How much does Cigna pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Evernorth revenue rose from $131,912 million in 2021 to $234,953 million in 2025. Adjusted income rose from $5,818 million in 2021 to $7,221 million in 2025. The key turn is adjusted revenue margin: 3.1% in 2025 versus 3.5% in 2024. Diluted shares fell 5.2% in 2025, while dividends per share reached $6.00 and buybacks per share were $13.48.

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $6.70 to $8.10 per share in the base case. The bear case holds at $6.10, while the bull case reaches $9.10. The base follows roughly 10% annual growth from the implied 2026 run rate, supported by a five-year record of increases from $4.00 to $6.04.

The bear freeze reflects weak cash conversion, debt service and regulated capital limits. The bull path assumes cash generation near the upper end of management’s ambition, although the company’s EPS target is not a dividend commitment.

blocks.heading: What is Cigna's dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: Debt narrows the room for error because cash used for interest, repayment and insurance capital cannot also fund buybacks. Management still expected debt capitalization to move closer to its 40% target. The 2.1% dividend yield is tangible, but its support depends on multi-year cash generation after debt and regulatory capital needs.

earnings.title: Cigna earnings: date, guidance and results
earnings.meta_description: Cigna reports results on November 5, 2026; see its guidance, recent earnings trend and what to watch.
earnings.opening: Cigna's next results are expected on November 5, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether Pharmacy Benefit Services’ earnings pressure is easing.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Cigna’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The company reaffirmed a target of at least $30.45 in adjusted earnings per share for 2026. Earnings per share divides profit among shareholders; adjusted earnings remove items management considers less representative of normal operations. In the second quarter, ordinary profit was $6.29 per share, while adjusted profit was $7.78 because Cigna excluded items such as acquired-intangible amortization, investment results and special charges. That can clarify recurring performance, but restructuring still costs real money.

Cigna Healthcare, the insurance business, is expected to provide at least $4,550 million of pre-tax adjusted operating income. Evernorth, which houses pharmacy and care services, is expected to provide at least $6,900 million. Yet pharmacy revenue rose 8% in the second quarter while Pharmacy Benefit Services’ adjusted operating income fell 27%. More prescriptions or more expensive drugs can increase revenue without increasing the fee left as profit.

blocks.heading: Did Cigna keep its earnings promise?

paragraphs.text: Cigna did meet its shorter promise. Management guided to at least $29.60 in full-year adjusted earnings per share and delivered $29.84. “Adjusted” means Cigna excludes specified items from accounting profit, so meeting that target does not erase a miss on a longer-term measure.

blocks.heading: How have Cigna's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: Core earnings increased about 6.4% from the prior year, while remaining almost unchanged from March. The quarterly series therefore suggests moderate improvement, not a steadily accelerating business.

Evernorth’s divisions moved in opposite directions. Pharmacy Benefit Services generated $34,496 million of revenue and $609 million of adjusted income. Specialty and Care Services produced $1,054 million of income. Drug mix lifted pharmacy revenue even as pharmacy activity declined, while specialty results benefited from Shields and operating efficiencies.
